claims.text: Controlled thermo-mechanical processing or directional solidification can align coherent nanoprecipitates along the principal heat-flow direction in a high-entropy-alloy intermediate layer.
Directional solidification can produce a directional, columnar, or single-crystal microstructure in a high-entropy alloy.
Directional alignment of coherent nanoprecipitates will establish continuous thermal-conduction channels.
The proposed continuous channels will enhance heat-transfer capability.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces can maintain mechanical integrity by facilitating deformation and relieving stress concentrations associated with premature crack initiation.
Current high-entropy-alloy intermediate layers have randomly distributed nanoprecipitates.
Current high-entropy-alloy intermediate layers have only moderate thermal conductivity.
Current high-entropy-alloy intermediate layers have adequate mechanical strength.
Plasma-facing reactor components encounter high temperature and high heat flux.
An intermediate layer is needed between a tungsten plasma-facing material and a CuCrZr heat sink because their suitable operating-temperature ranges differ.
The proposed benefit will persist under the high mechanical loading typical of plasma-facing reactor operation.
Aligned coherent nanoprecipitates will form interconnected high-conductivity pathways.
Coherent interfaces will preserve load transfer in the engineered intermediate layer.
Alignment will boost phonon transport along the proposed precipitate channels.
Coherent interfaces will mitigate crack propagation under reactor-relevant loading.
The aligned microstructure will produce a significant increase in thermal conductivity relative to a random-precipitate baseline.
The aligned microstructure will cause no substantial loss of strength or ductility at reactor-relevant temperatures and loads.
Conventional processing yields a random precipitate distribution that only moderately balances heat transfer and mechanical performance.
Departures from the intended temperature, loading, or processing quality may diminish the proposed benefits.
